keyVerseText: And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age.
rootMeaning: The root word שֵׂיב (sêyb, H7869) conveys the concept of age, specifically hoary or gray-headed age, emphasizing the visible signs of aging such as gray hair. The feminine form שֵׂיבָה (sêybâh, H7872) carries this meaning forward, focusing on gray hairs or old age as a natural stage of life. This root sense enriches the common English gloss of 'old age' by highlighting the physical manifestation of aging—the gray or hoary head—which symbolizes wisdom and the passage of time.
usageInScripture: The word שֵׂיבָה appears 19 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently referring to old age or gray hairs. Its translations range from 'old age' (most frequent) to more specific phrases like 'my gray hairs,' 'the hoary head,' and 'of thine old age,' indicating both literal and figurative uses. This consistency underscores the term's strong association with the dignity and respect due to advanced years, as well as the natural progression toward life's end.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שֵׂיבָה in its original sense reminds believers that aging is a divinely ordained process marked by honor and reverence. The gray head symbolizes accumulated wisdom and experience, reflecting God's sustaining grace throughout a lifetime. This word invites the faithful to see old age not as decline but as a blessed stage, culminating in peace and fulfillment under God's providence. It also points to the hope of a peaceful end, assured by God's promises to His people.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 15:15 states, 'And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age.' Here, שֵׂיבָה conveys more than mere longevity; it expresses a blessed completion of life marked by peace and divine favor. The phrase 'good old age' highlights the quality and dignity of the years lived, assuring believers that God honors those who walk faithfully with Him until their final rest.
